transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (calculated)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood CSM), Priya (Velaris Eng), Mark (Velaris Platform), Sasha (Velaris PM), Omar (Velaris SRE)

Summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
Quick sync on week 4 pilot results, confirm canary thresholds and A/B routing percentages. Plan staging dry-run and agree owners for runbook items. Discussed telemetry gaps and one regression in latency tail for longer prompts.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, thanks for hopping on. Intent for today is to lock down the release runway and A/B split. I got a quick agenda, hope that's fine.
[00:22] Priya (Velaris Eng): Yeah that's good. We had one perf blip on Friday so we wanna make sure the canary catches that.
[00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Quick note: that perf blip looked like KV cache warmup + a rare scheduling hiccup when batch sizes spiked, so we think it's mitigatable with a short warmup window.
[00:44] Mark (Velaris): Can you run through what metrics you suggest we gate on? We need concrete numbers to share with execs.
[00:52] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure—primary SLO is p95 latency under 350ms for our 512-token average; secondary is error rate under 0.2% and median cost delta within expected. We'll propose canary alarm at p95 >= 400ms for two consecutive 5-min buckets.
[01:18] Sasha (Velaris PM): Two questions: one, how do we measure A/B quality for the product team? Two, who owns the experiment dashboard?
[01:25] Maya (Redwood AE): Good call. For quality, we recommend a small offline eval set (the top 10 queries Priya mentioned) and realtime basic QA metrics—token counts, repetition, hallucination flags from our eval hook. Ownership: Redwood can host the dashboard but Velaris will be given a dashboard link and alert rights.
[01:40] Priya (Velaris Eng): I can share those queries after the call, will put context around expected outputs.
[01:46] Omar (Velaris SRE): On alerts—we need an alert route into PagerDuty and Slack. Do you support multiple webhook targets?
[01:53] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, we can route to multiple endpoints; we'll send a sample alert config.
[02:02] Hannah (Redwood CSM): I'll include the contact list and escalation order in the runbook doc.
[02:10] Mark (Velaris): For the A/B split, what would you recommend as a default traffic ramp? We don't want to be too aggressive.
[02:18] Diego (Redwood SE): Typical is 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over discrete windows with steady-state checks at each step. But because you have critical user flows, I'd suggest a more conservative 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30%.
[02:34] Priya (Velaris Eng): Can the platform pin model variants for the B lane? We want to test a quantized variant against the baseline.
[02:42] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes—pinning is supported. We can also set fallback rules so if B exceeds latency threshold, traffic automatically shifts back to A.
[02:52] Priya (Velaris Eng): Nice. What about data retention and logs—how long do you keep request/response traces?
[03:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Default is 90 days for basic telemetry; audit exports for enterprise are configurable—Hannah will send the SOC2 summary and the log export options.
[03:12] Mark (Velaris): We need an audit log CSV for compliance; can you confirm export format?
[03:18] Hannah (Redwood CSM): We'll send the sample export schema after this call.
[03:24] Sasha (Velaris PM): During Friday's blip we also saw a small uptick in token usage for a subset of customers—did Redwood's batching change anything?
[03:34] Diego (Redwood SE): No, batching shouldn't increase token counts—it might alter per-request latency. The uptick might be due to a prompt template change on your side; worth checking.
[03:44] Priya (Velaris Eng): We'll double-check templates.
[03:48] Maya (Redwood AE): For the runbook—Diego, can you outline the quick rollback steps? We want a one-page checklist for oncall.
[03:56] Diego (Redwood SE): Absolutely. Step 1: Pause traffic to B lane via routing gate. Step 2: Scale down B replicas (if dedicated) and revert routing. Step 3: If root cause not obvious, roll back to previously pinned model version. Step 4: Open incident in our joint channel and attach logs. I'll add exact API calls.
[04:20] Omar (Velaris SRE): Are those API calls documented? We need a runbook we can run from terminal.
[04:26] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll provide curl/examples and a small runbook script.
[04:32] Priya (Velaris Eng): For the canary metric alarm threshold you suggested—two consecutive five-minute buckets at p95 >= 400ms—do we want to add an error-rate check too? If error rate jumps a little but latency is okay, we still care.
[04:48] Diego (Redwood SE): Good point. We'll make it a composite alarm: p95 >= 400ms OR error_rate >= 0.5% for two consecutive windows.
[04:58] Hannah (Redwood CSM): I'll include the composite alarm in the doc.
[05:04] Sasha (Velaris PM): On the A/B evaluation—how are we computing sample size? We need significance for subjective metrics.
[05:12] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll share recommended sample sizes (statistical guidance) but for launch you can set pragmatic thresholds—if qualitative regressions on the golden queries exceed X, stop the rollout.
[05:24] Priya (Velaris Eng): What's X?
[05:26] Maya (Redwood AE): For now propose 3 regressions out of top 10 queries or any critical-flow failure. We'll tune post-dry-run.
[05:36] Mark (Velaris): Who owns the experiment analysis? Redwood or Velaris?
[05:40] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll provide the analysis template and initial pass; Velaris owns the final go/no-go based on your business rules.
[05:48] Omar (Velaris SRE): Can we run a staging dry-run with a synthetic load that mirrors real session lengths? I can prepare the load profile.
[05:56] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, and also include cold-start scenarios for short bursts so we exercise the KV warmup.
[06:04] Omar (Velaris SRE): I'll share the load file and expected QPS by tomorrow.
[06:08] Priya (Velaris Eng): About rollback windows—we want a quiet window during morning traffic to do the cutover. Is there an ops blackout?
[06:16] Sasha (Velaris PM): Morning traffic is lighter on weekends. We were thinking Sunday 02:00 UTC but need to confirm with execs.
[06:24] Maya (Redwood AE): That works for the rollback window. We'll note timezones in the runbook.
[06:30] Mark (Velaris): Any outstanding security items? SSO and RBAC are set up but we need SAML assertion mapping for roles.
[06:38] Hannah (Redwood CSM): We sent the SAML mapping guide last week; I'll re-share and add the Velaris attribute map template.
[06:46] Priya (Velaris Eng): How do we access raw request traces if we need to debug?
[06:50] Diego (Redwood SE): We'll enable limited trace access for your SRE role and deliver a secure S3 export for full payloads under NDA.
[06:58] Priya (Velaris Eng): NDA is in process.
[07:02] Maya (Redwood AE): Ok circling back—diego you'll own runbook + rollback steps, Hannah will send SOC2/export schema, Omar will provide load file, Priya will provide golden queries. Agree?
[07:12] (crosstalk) Priya: yes, yes. Diego: yep.
[07:20] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. Let's talk about the A/B traffic percentages again—Velaris, what's your confidence in customers tolerating variation?
[07:30] Sasha (Velaris PM): We have telemetry that shows 95% of flows are tolerant, but a small set of premium customers need near-zero degradation. We want them excluded from experiments.
[07:40] Diego (Redwood SE): We can do targeted routing to exclude customer IDs or user cohorts. We'll add exclusion rules into the rollout config.
[07:50] Mark (Velaris): Perfect. Also, if the B lane is quantized and cheaper, how do billing and cost attribution look during A/B?
[07:58] Maya (Redwood AE): We provide token-level cost breakdown per model variant and per route. We'll put together a cost delta spreadsheet for the pilot.
[08:08] Priya (Velaris Eng): One last technical question—when B falls back to A, do KV caches get warm again? That's where we saw tail latency.
[08:16] Diego (Redwood SE): The fallback preserves some prefixes for pinned models but a full warmup may be needed; we'll recommend a short warmup window and synthetic priming traffic as part of the runbook.
[08:28] Omar (Velaris SRE): Sounds good.
[08:32] Maya (Redwood AE): Ok, let's capture next steps. Diego will deliver the runbook checklist and sample API commands by Wednesday (2026-11-18). Priya will send golden queries by tomorrow. Omar shares load file by tomorrow. Hannah shares SOC2 summary and export schema by Thursday. Redwood will supply the canary dashboard link and initial alert configs by Wednesday.
[08:56] Sasha (Velaris PM): Thanks all. If we can get the dry-run scheduled for Friday (2026-11-20) that'd be ideal.
[09:02] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll put a calendar hold after this call.
[09:06] (brief off-mic chatter)
[09:12] Maya (Redwood AE): Any final questions?
[09:16] Mark (Velaris): None from me.
[09:18] Priya (Velaris Eng): All good.
[09:20] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. We'll follow up with links and the runbook doc. Thanks everyone.

Post-call notes (auto): Links referenced - runbook draft (redwood.com/velaris/runbook-draft), canary dashboard (redwood.com/velaris/canary-dashboard) — placeholder links, SOC2 summary doc (redwood.com/compliance/soc2-summary).
